summary: Full published-paper extraction checkpoint with 136 interfaces, exact fixed-determinant and iterated-Frobenius conventions, four coordinated Part II proposals and existing-foundation source routes. It extracts nilpotent reductions, crystalline realizations and periodic flows, geometric p-adic rigidity, unitarity and cohomologically rigid companions. Status remains partial: a concrete nonreduced-family BNR obstruction and other independently unreviewed proof findings, external-source closure and Frobenius/representation normalization gates remain. No Lean implementation, proof closure or confirmed author erratum is claimed.

items.name: Rigid stable connection with fixed determinant
items.statement: In convention C, rigidity means that the isomorphism class is an isolated point of the moduli of P-stable rank-r integrable connections with the specified determinant (L,∇L). It does not require the isolated point to be reduced. Rank-one characters cannot be varied while forgetting the determinant condition.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Cohomological rigidity
items.statement: In C, cohomological rigidity means H¹_dR(X,End⁰(E,∇))=0, where End⁰ is the kernel of trace. Equivalently the fixed-determinant moduli point is reduced and isolated. Use the trace-free statement on p.148, not the unqualified End printed on p.106; see E1.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Stable Betti, de Rham and Dolbeault moduli
items.statement: For smooth projective X with polarization, fixed rank, Hilbert polynomial/Chern-class component and torsion determinant, construct the stable representation, connection and trace-free Higgs moduli used here. State the characteristic-zero vanishing rational Chern classes needed for the Simpson component. Over arithmetic bases use Langer's moduli, with geometric-point base-change rather than an unproved arbitrary-base-change isomorphism.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Integrable Higgs bundle
items.statement: For smooth Z/T, a Higgs bundle is a finite locally free O_Z-module V with O_Z-linear θ:V→V⊗Ω¹_Z/T satisfying θ∧θ=0. Morphisms commute with θ. Scaling, tensor, dual and determinant must be constructed; trace-zero is the fixed-determinant subproblem, not part of the general definition.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Relative integrable connection
items.statement: For smooth Z/T, a connection on a finite-type module E is an O_T-linear ∇:E→E⊗Ω¹_Z/T satisfying ∇(fe)=f∇e+e⊗df; integrability is ∇²=0 in E⊗Ω². Distinguish all such connections from their quasi-nilpotent subcategory. The generic algebraic connection carrier belongs to CR.1; the complex moduli and positive-characteristic transforms import it.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Simpson correspondence in the projective component
items.statement: In C, stable Higgs bundles with vanishing rational Chern classes correspond to irreducible flat connections, compatibly with the torsion determinant. The induced moduli correspondence is real analytic, preserves isolated points and hence gives equality of the finite counts of rigid objects. This is not an equivalence between all Higgs bundles and all connections in positive characteristic.

items.name: Riemann–Hilbert comparison
items.statement: For smooth projective complex X, analytification and horizontal sections identify algebraic integrable connections with complex local systems; the stable fixed-determinant Betti and de Rham moduli are analytically identified. Preserve the topological versus étale fundamental groups and do not assert an algebraic isomorphism of these moduli.

items.name: Rigid Higgs fields are nilpotent
items.statement: A rigid stable trace-free Higgs bundle on smooth projective complex X has nilpotent Higgs field: its Hitchin coefficients have positive G_m-weights, so a nonzero coefficient would yield a nonconstant family of moduli points under scaling.

items.name: Ring derivation carrier
items.statement: For a commutative R-algebra A and compatible A-module M, an R-derivation is an R-linear map A→M satisfying D(1)=0 and D(ab)=aD(b)+bD(a). This is the affine carrier only, not a sheaf of restricted Lie algebroids or a connection on a module.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Characteristic-p iterate of a derivation
items.statement: For a k-derivation δ of a commutative k-algebra in characteristic p, δ iterated p times is again a derivation. Sheafify this to the restricted p-operation δ^[p] on Θ_Z/k. The p-operation is composition of operators, not multiplication of values.

items.name: Relative Frobenius and twisted variety
items.statement: For smooth Z over perfect k of characteristic p, form Z'=Z×_{k,F_k}k, projection w:Z'→Z and relative F:Z→Z', with absolute Frobenius w∘F. w is an isomorphism of schemes but generally not of k-schemes; define the analogous twist for relative families and track the base parameter separately.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: p-curvature operator
items.statement: In P, ψ∇(δ)=(∇δ)^p−∇_{δ^[p]}. Its target is End_O(E). Define it from the connection action on vector fields; do not use ∇^p as an exterior differential or confuse the tensor-iterated nilpotency with ∇²=0.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Additive Frobenius-semilinear p-curvature
items.statement: For an integrable connection in characteristic p, ψ(δ₁+fδ₂)=ψ(δ₁)+f^pψ(δ₂), and ψ(δ) is O-linear. These identities descend to the relative Frobenius twist, including their compatibility under pullback where the relative constructions exist.

items.name: Frobenius pushforward p-curvature Higgs field
items.statement: The p-curvature of E determines an O_Z'-linear Higgs field on F_*E with values Ω¹_Z'; use F-semilinearity and the projection formula. If Z is smooth pure dimension d and E has rank r, F_*E has rank rp^d. Integrability and this rank multiplication are separate verified properties.
items.locator: Lemma–Definition 2.6 p.111; proof of Theorem 2.17 p.118

uses.where: Lemma–Definition 2.6 p.111; proof of Theorem 2.17 p.118

items.name: Tensor-iterated nilpotency
items.statement: A Higgs field or p-curvature is nilpotent when some N-fold tensor iterate is zero. Use the paper's convention θ^N=0 (respectively ψ^N=0) for Higgs_N and MIC_N. Record the translation to sources that call this level N−1; the exterior-square integrability condition alone does not give nilpotency.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Gauss–Manin p-curvature is nilpotent
items.statement: For a smooth projective morphism f:Y→Z of smooth varieties over perfect k of characteristic p, the Gauss–Manin connection on relative algebraic de Rham cohomology R^if_*(O_Y,d) has nilpotent p-curvature in the finite-type/coherent sense of Katz. Do not infer zero p-curvature.

items.name: Crystalline differential operators
items.statement: On smooth Z/k construct the universal enveloping algebra of the tangent Lie algebroid, generated by O_Z and Θ_Z with [δ,f]=δ(f) and [δ,η] the vector-field bracket. This is the crystalline D_Z, not the full divided-power differential-operator algebra; construct the equivalence with O-quasi-coherent modules carrying integrable connections.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Centre of crystalline differential operators
items.statement: For smooth Z over perfect k, the map Sym_O_Z'(Θ_Z')→F_*D_Z induced by δ↦δ^p−δ^[p] is injective and identifies the source with the centre. Its degree-one elements act on a connection by p-curvature.

items.name: Cotangent Azumaya sheaf
items.statement: For π:T*Z'→Z', use affine quasi-coherent descent to construct the O_T*Z'-algebra 𝒟 whose pushforward is F_*D_Z, using the central Sym Θ_Z' action. The equality π_*𝒟=F_*D_Z is part of the construction, not a choice of an arbitrary matrix algebra.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: D-module and cotangent-module equivalence
items.statement: The category of quasi-coherent D_Z-modules is equivalent to quasi-coherent 𝒟-modules on T*Z'. Construct both directions through the affine morphisms F and π, including the induced Higgs operator on π_*M.

items.name: Azumaya algebra over a ring
items.statement: For a commutative ring R and R-algebra A, IsAzumaya requires A finite, projective and faithful over R and bijectivity of A⊗_R A^op→End_R(A), a⊗b↦(x↦axb). This ring predicate already exists; its equivalence with étale-local matrix splittings and its scheme descent are separate items.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Geometric Azumaya and splitting-module interface
items.statement: Construct Azumaya O_Y-algebras locally using the existing ring predicate, their étale-local matrix splittings, splitting modules and change-of-splitting invertible bimodules. Over a strictly henselian local ring the finite-rank Azumaya algebra splits; ordinary henselianity without a residue-field splitting condition is insufficient.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Morita equivalence with coherent support
items.statement: For a split Azumaya algebra End_R(P), P finite projective faithfully generating, construct equivalence M↦P⊗_R M with inverse Hom_A(P,−). In the free rank-n case the underlying R-module is M^⊕n. Track finite local freeness after affine pushforward, annihilator ideals and changes of splitting; no claim of a unique isomorphism between arbitrary isomorphic modules.

items.name: BMR Azumaya theorem and rank
items.statement: For smooth pure d-dimensional Z over perfect k of characteristic p, the cotangent algebra 𝒟 is Azumaya of O-rank p^(2d), étale-locally End(O^(p^d)). Distinguish algebra rank from splitting-module rank.

items.name: Cartier descent at zero p-curvature
items.statement: For smooth Z/k with k perfect, F^* with canonical connection is fully faithful from quasi-coherent O_Z'-modules to integrable connections, and its essential image consists exactly of zero-p-curvature connections. The inverse is horizontal sections on the twist.

items.name: Bounded nilpotent categories
items.statement: Construct full subcategories Higgs_N(Z') and MIC_N(Z) using item 015, their morphisms and finite-locally-free subcategories. Bounds must be supplied before using inverse Cartier; do not define all nilpotent objects to be automatically in the p-bounded range.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Ogus–Vologodsky inverse Cartier
items.statement: For smooth Z/k, k perfect of characteristic p, and a specified W₂(k)-lift, construct the inverse Cartier equivalence from the permitted nilpotent Higgs category on Z' to nilpotent connections on Z. On θ=0 it agrees with item 025. Pin the level translation in 015 and the chosen lift/sign; prove splitting over the permitted infinitesimal zero-section neighborhood before using families.

items.name: Prime-to-p determinant transport
items.statement: For a torsion line bundle L of order prime to p, relative Frobenius pullback of its twist agrees with L^p; inverse Cartier of the zero Higgs determinant has that underlying determinant. Exponentiation by p permutes the powers L^a for a modulo ord(L), so counting must either follow that permutation or range over the entire finite determinant orbit.

items.name: Horizontal p-curvature coefficients
items.statement: The p-curvature is horizontal for the canonical Frobenius-pullback connection tensored with End(∇). Hence its characteristic coefficients descend to a_i∈H⁰(Z',Sym^iΩ¹_Z'); in the determinant-zero-p-curvature component a₁=0.

items.name: Trace-free p-curvature Hitchin morphism
items.statement: Construct χ_dR:M_dR(Z,L^p,r)→A_Z',r with A=⊕_{i=2}^r H⁰(Z',Sym^iΩ¹). Associate the monic trace-free degree-r expression λ^r+∑_{i=2}^r(−1)^i a_iλ^(r−i). Its coefficients, not all degree-r sections, parametrize A. χ_dR=0 iff p-curvature is nilpotent.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Proper p-curvature Hitchin map in the moduli category
items.statement: Record Langer's properness theorem in its semistable moduli setting, together with the restriction used for the stable locus. Verify the exact base, Hilbert-polynomial and determinant hypotheses in [Lan] Theorem 3.8 before asserting properness of an open stable subspace; this extraction does not silently transfer properness across that open immersion.

items.name: Higher-dimensional spectral subscheme
items.statement: For a family a:S→A, evaluate the monic characteristic expression on the tautological cotangent section; define Z'_a in T*Z'×S by all components of the resulting Sym^rπ*Ω¹-valued section. It is finite over Z'×S. In dimension greater than one do not replace this vector-valued equation by one scalar polynomial or assert flat degree r without proof.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Family BNR forward functor
items.statement: For an S-family of rank-r integrable connections with χ_dR=a, associate a 𝒟-module M scheme-theoretically supported on Z'_a, with π_*M locally free rank rp^d and Higgs characteristic polynomial a^(p^d). The refined support/descent assertion over nonreduced S requires item 035 and the repair gate E2. Use the strengthened invariant condition of 034 for the converse.

items.name: Family BNR inverse and essential image
items.statement: Corrected target for arbitrary S: require that the characteristic polynomial of each local rank-r Morita reduction is a, not merely that π_*M has polynomial a^(p^d) and M is supported on Z'_a. With independence and descent from 035 proved, reconstruct the connection and the inverse correspondence. The printed weaker right-hand conditions admit the rank-three zero-operator counterexample over dual numbers described in E2.

items.name: Morita characteristic polynomial gluing
items.statement: For the local Morita reductions of the BNR module, prove independence of splitting, descent of the rank-r characteristic polynomial, and annihilation by its spectral ideal. Use transition bimodules or the actual p-curvature invariant, not injectivity of Frobenius on arbitrary coefficient rings. This is the precise missing proof interface behind E2.

items.name: Scheme-theoretic module support
items.statement: For a closed immersion i:Y→T and quasi-coherent algebra-module M on T, support on Y means I_Y·M=0. It depends on the underlying O_T-module, and is stronger than topological support on |Y|. Use it under Morita equivalence and base change.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: p-typical Witt vector coefficient carrier
items.statement: Use WittVector p k for p-typical Witt vectors; coefficients indexed by natural numbers determine the element. The coefficient ring, not a new geometric-crystal carrier, is the input to W(k)-lifts.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Witt Frobenius equivalence
items.statement: For a perfect commutative ring k of characteristic p, WittVector.frobeniusEquiv is a ring automorphism of W(k), with nth coefficient sent to its pth power. This is coefficient Frobenius only, not Frobenius on a sheaf or a crystalline cohomology complex.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Pointwise semilinear isocrystal carrier
items.statement: Over a perfect characteristic-p domain k, the existing WittVector.Isocrystal is a Frac(W(k))-vector space with a Frobenius-semilinear automorphism. It supplies the pointwise linear-algebra notion only; geometric isocrystals on Z and F^f-structures for arbitrary f are not credited by this declaration.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Small crystalline sites over truncated Witt rings
items.statement: For smooth Z/k and W_n=W(k)/p^n, construct the crystalline site from PD thickenings (U,T,δ) compatible with the base PD structure and its structure sheaf; retain the chosen topology and finite-type module convention. Construct the embeddings of sites as n increases.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Crystals and pullback isomorphisms
items.statement: A finite-type crystal has O_T-modules on PD thickenings and isomorphisms f^*F_T₂≅F_T₁ for every site morphism, satisfying functoriality. Construct Crys(Z/W_n), Crys(Z/W) and their exact/abelian structures under the paper's smoothness assumptions; do not confuse crystal transition maps with only restriction along opens.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Geometric isocrystals and iterated Frobenius structures
items.statement: Form Crys(Z/W)_Q. A Frobenius structure here is an isomorphism (F^f)^*E≅E for some specified f>0, potentially after finite residue-field extension. Neither an integral Frobenius lattice nor an f=1 structure is automatic from the definition.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Quasi-nilpotent connection on a smooth lift
items.statement: On a smooth W_n-lift, use coordinate-wise eventual annihilation by sufficiently high differential operators, in the crystalline topological/quasi-nilpotence convention. Establish coordinate independence; it is not the condition that each connection matrix be nilpotent.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Quasi-nilpotence detected on the special fibre
items.statement: For a finite-type connection on a smooth W_n-lift, quasi-nilpotence is equivalent to quasi-nilpotence after reduction mod p, by iterating annihilation through the finite p-power filtration. On smooth Z/k the latter is equivalent to nilpotent p-curvature.

items.name: Finite-level crystals versus nilpotent p-curvature
items.statement: For a smooth formal W(k)-lift Zhat with Z_n its W_n reduction, evaluation gives Crys(Z/W_n)≃ the full subcategory of finite-type integrable connections on Z_n whose special-fibre p-curvature is nilpotent.

items.name: Complete formal connections versus crystals
items.statement: For the same formal lift, Crys(Z/W) is equivalent to finite-type integrable connections E≅lim_n E/p^nE which are separated and complete and have nilpotent special-fibre p-curvature. Both completeness and the inverse-limit comparison must be proved.

items.name: Arithmetic connection gives a crystal
items.statement: For smooth X/W(k) and an integrable connection whose restriction to the special fibre has nilpotent p-curvature, its formal completion defines a crystal. Applied to the model of Theorem 1.4 and a W(k)-point in the permitted locus, this is Corollary 1.5.

items.name: Smooth arithmetic model
items.statement: In C, choose an integral affine S smooth finite type over Z with function field embedded in C, a smooth projective X_S/S and a line bundle L_S pulling back to X,L. Spread the torsion relation and its flat structure and invert the determinant order as needed. Each subsequent shrinking must retain a nonempty generic fibre.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Relative rigid locus
items.statement: For a finite-type morphism Y→S, Y^rig is the maximal open where the morphism is quasi-finite. For the stable de Rham/Dolbeault moduli this gives the relative locus of isolated geometric-fibre points, including their possible nonreduced local schemes.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Simultaneous spreading of rigid objects
items.statement: For fixed r and torsion determinant, finitely many rigid complex connections and Higgs bundles of rank ≤r can all be spread over one arithmetic model, remaining geometrically P-stable. Finiteness follows from isolated components of a finite-type moduli scheme, not from all stable objects being finite in number.

items.name: Nilpotent and relatively rigid models
items.statement: After shrinking the model in item 050, the spread Higgs fields remain nilpotent and all chosen connection/Higgs sections factor through their relative rigid loci. Openness of stability and of the quasi-finite locus are separate inputs.

items.name: Rigid loci exhausted by spread sections
items.statement: After further shrinking, the geometric points of every rigid fibre are supplied by the finitely many spread sections; use Zariski's main theorem and remove the image of the finite-completion boundary. For later counting choose the sections disjoint after shrinking. Retain the local-scheme lengths, not just the reduced points.

items.name: Rigidity preserved by Frobenius twist
items.statement: For smooth projective Z over perfect k, w^* identifies families on Z with appropriately twisted families on Z'; it preserves stability and rigidity for both Higgs bundles and integrable connections. The family parameter scheme is twisted as well.

items.name: OV-admissible Hitchin family
items.statement: For a:T→A_Z',r, OV-admissibility means that its spectral subscheme factors through the infinitesimal zero-section neighborhood on which the chosen Ogus–Vologodsky splitting is defined. Keep the paper's p−1 order convention explicit; p≥r+2 is a standing sufficient large-rank bound here.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Uniform infinitesimal support bound
items.statement: Construct the polynomial R(r,m), linear in m and quadratic in r as asserted in Proposition 3.5, such that p−1>R(r,m) makes every A^(m)-valued Hitchin family OV-admissible. A design must supply a proven explicit bound from the component spectral ideal, not just a field naming this existential claim.

items.name: Inverse Cartier preserves stability in the needed range
items.statement: For a nice arithmetic model, sufficiently large p and a stable rigid nilpotent Higgs bundle on the twisted fibre, inverse Cartier is stable. Verify the stability argument beyond Langer's quoted semistability result and retain the nilpotency/rank/degree hypotheses.

items.name: Inverse Cartier preserves rigidity for large p
items.statement: There is D depending on the fixed nice model such that, for closed s of characteristic p>D, inverse Cartier of a rigid stable Higgs bundle is a rigid stable connection. Proof uses finite lengths of rigid loci, family BNR, the support bound and a deformation truncation. Gate the nonreduced descent and jet-order steps by E2 and E3 rather than crediting proof closure.

items.name: Counts of rigid objects and nilpotent subset
items.statement: For smooth projective Z/k and torsion determinant of order invertible in k, let n_dR and n_Dol count geometric isomorphism classes of stable rigid rank-r objects in the specified determinant component; n_dR^nilp counts the nilpotent-p-curvature subset. Count all determinant powers when transporting by Frobenius.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Counting forces nilpotent p-curvature
items.statement: If the relevant de Rham and twisted Dolbeault rigid counts agree, and inverse Cartier gives an injection from the latter to nilpotent rigid connections with the correctly transported determinant, then n_dR^nilp=n_dR. Equal finite cardinalities, not essential surjectivity assumed in advance, supply the conclusion.

items.name: Nilpotent reductions of rigid complex connections
items.statement: In C there is a finite-type arithmetic model after shrinking such that every closed-fibre connection has nilpotent p-curvature. Uniformity is over the closed points of this chosen model; no claim for all primes or all models. Derive the count equality using Simpson and specialization of the finite rigid loci, then item 059.

items.name: Integrable lambda-connection
items.statement: For regular λ on a smooth base, a λ-connection satisfies D(fs)=fD(s)+λs⊗df and D²=0. The fibres λ=0 and λ=1 are Higgs bundles and ordinary connections respectively. Define Griffiths-transverse filtrations and their associated graded Higgs fields before forming a flow.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Hodge moduli and its rigid locus
items.statement: Construct M_Hod→A¹ of P-stable λ-connections with fixed torsion determinant; its fibres at 0,1 are M_Dol,M_dR. Define its relative quasi-finite locus and the G_m-action compatible with the parameter.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Rigid Hodge family splits over A1
items.statement: For smooth projective complex X, the rigid Hodge locus is finite flat over A¹ and G_m-equivariantly isomorphic to M_Dol^rig×A¹. Use Simpson's étale-local product statement and the G_m splitting off zero, retaining the nonreduced structure; this is stronger than a bijection of closed points.

items.name: Rigid connections underlie complex variations
items.statement: In C a rigid stable connection underlies a complex variation of Hodge structure; the associated graded of its Griffiths-transverse filtration is the corresponding stable Higgs bundle. The filtration is unique up to shift in the rigid situation. A complex variation need not have a real or integral structure, so do not insert a lattice into its definition.

items.name: Nice Hodge models for the determinant orbit
items.statement: Spread the finitely many rigid Hodge families simultaneously over a smooth affine arithmetic S, for ranks ≤r and all L^a with 0≤a<d=ord(L), maintaining geometric stability and exhaustion by their sections. Normalize the inconsistent S/A¹ and determinant-power indices in the printed formulas as in E9.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Signed inverse Cartier flow functor
items.statement: Define I₁=C⁻¹∘(w⁻¹)^*∘ι from Higgs bundles on Z to connections on Z, where ι(V,θ)=(V,−θ). Pin twist direction and sign in coordinates. Use one name for this inverse Cartier functor: Definition 4.1(b) labels it C₁ while subsequent formulas use C₁⁻¹ (E8).

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Higgs–de Rham fixed point
items.statement: A fixed point is (H,∇,Fil,φ) with a nilpotent flat bundle, a descending Griffiths-transverse filtration in the permitted range and an isomorphism I₁(gr_Fil(H,∇))≅(H,∇). Filtration shifts, morphisms and compatibility with the graded operation are data to specify.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Periodic flat connection in characteristic p
items.statement: An f-periodic object consists of f filtered nilpotent flat bundles indexed by Z/fZ and isomorphisms I₁(gr(E_i,∇_i,Fil_i))≅(E_{i+1},∇_{i+1}); f>0. Their direct sum is a fixed point with the coefficient endomorphism structure needed for the F_(p^f) realization. Periodic means every point is on a cycle, not merely eventually periodic.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Finite-coefficient realization of a periodic flow
items.statement: If smooth Z/k lifts to smooth Z_W/W(k), k contains F_(p^f), and the flow satisfies the precise LSZ/SYZ bounds, the category of f-periodic flows has a fully faithful realization in F_(p^f)-étale local systems on Z_K. Verify the endpoint subcategory and filtration range in the external source; do not infer unrestricted full faithfulness at p−1 from its notation.

items.name: Mixed-characteristic input H(Zn/Wn)
items.statement: For n≥1, keep a graded Higgs bundle (V,θ) over Z_n together with a filtered connection (E,∇,Fil) over Z_(n−1) and an identified reduction (V,θ)_(n−1)≅gr_Fil(E,∇). Require nilpotent special-fibre level in the p−2 range and the locally split filtration hypotheses of the source. Treat n=1 through I₁ rather than an undefined nontrivial Z₀ connection.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Higher inverse Cartier functors
items.statement: Construct I_n:H(Z_n/W_n)→MIC(Z_n/W_n), compatible under reduction and extending I₁. The previous filtered level and comparison isomorphism are essential input: a bare Higgs bundle mod p^n does not specify this functor.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Periodic flat connection over a Witt lift
items.statement: An f-periodic object on Z_W is f filtered flat bundles with compatible level-n isomorphisms I_n(gr(E_i,∇_i,Fil_i))≅(E_{i+1},∇_{i+1}) for all n, and p−2-bounded special fibre; assume k⊃F_(p^f). Do not substitute only the n=1 isomorphism for compatible mixed-characteristic data.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Fixed flows and relative Fontaine–Laffaille modules
items.statement: Under the LSZ/SYZ smooth-lift and filtration hypotheses, 1-periodic filtered connections correspond to torsion-free relative Fontaine–Laffaille modules/strongly p-divisible lattices on Z_W. Import the absolute point theory from R07.3; the relative connection and descent enhancement is additional, not already supplied by that layer.

items.name: Crystalline realization of mixed periodic flows
items.statement: Under the same hypotheses and k⊃F_(p^f), f-periodic connections give a fully faithful functor to crystalline étale local systems of finite free W(F_(p^f))-modules on Z_K. Keep the variance, Frobenius convention and filtration bounds source-qualified.

items.name: Periodic connection gives iterated Frobenius isocrystal
items.statement: The formal completion of a periodic W-family has an isocrystal with an F^f-structure after the required coefficient/residue-field extension. This forgets the stronger filtered integral structure but does not manufacture f=1 on the original object.

items.name: Permutation of the finite rigid set
items.statement: On the finite rigid set over all determinant powers, compose the graded-Hodge map, Frobenius twist and inverse Cartier to obtain σ. Show it is bijective using the corresponding inverse equivalences and the large-p rigidity assertion; the finite set includes every determinant component visited by pth powering.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Orbit periods of rigid flows
items.statement: For i in that finite set the Higgs–de Rham flow has period equal to the length of the σ-orbit. A common positive multiple f_r of these lengths bounds all periods in the fixed rank/determinant orbit; finiteness alone without bijectivity gives only eventual periodicity.
items.locator: Lemma 4.12(1) p.134; proof of Theorem 1.6 p.137

items.name: Independence from the W2 lift at the rigid-point level
items.statement: The W₂-lifts form an affine parameter space controlled by Kodaira–Spencer theory, and the family of Cartier correspondences induces a constant bijection on the finite set of rigid points. Thus the permutation and orbit periods do not depend on the chosen lift. This does not assert equality of all functors or nonreduced moduli schemes.

items.name: Rigid Witt points are determined by the special point
items.statement: For the selected nice model, each reduced connected rigid component is S. Since W(k) is reduced, reduction induces a bijection M_dR^rig(W(k))→M_dR^rig(k). This is not a bijection for arbitrary nonreduced W_i(k).

items.name: Unique rigid Hodge filtration at finite level
items.statement: A stable rigid W_i(k)-family has a Griffiths-transverse filtration unique up to shift; conversely a graded rigid Higgs family comes from the corresponding filtered connection up to isomorphism. Prove this from the spread equivariant Hodge-moduli splitting, including passage from coarse points to objects and stabilization of scalar automorphisms.

items.name: Forgetting higher inverse-Cartier input is bijective on rigid objects
items.statement: For the rigid stable subproblem over W_i, the forgetful map from tuples in H(Z_i/W_i) to rigid Higgs isomorphism classes is a bijection, using uniqueness of the preceding filtered connection and comparison map. Track grading shifts and scalar automorphisms in Claim 4.15 rather than treating coarse points as a fine moduli space.

items.name: Liftable finite-level rigid points
items.statement: For M_i=M_dR^rig(W/p^i), put M_i,0=intersection over j>i of image(M_j→M_i). The tower consists of finite sets when k is finite; prove its Mittag–Leffler/inverse-limit lifting property before asserting surjectivity M_W→M_i,0.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Bijections between liftable truncation levels
items.statement: The reduction M_(i+1),0→M_i,0 is a bijection: use the finite-tower lifting property and M_W≅M_1 from Claim 4.13. Do not replace M_i,0 by the generally larger M_i.

items.name: Flow preserves liftable finite-level points
items.statement: The higher flows commute with reduction M_(i+1)→M_i, and hence preserve every image from a higher level and M_i,0. This compatibility transports the special-fibre permutation to compatible Witt-level periodic flows.

items.name: Frobenius structure on rigid connections
items.statement: In C, after choosing a sufficiently small arithmetic model, every W(k)-point with k finite gives a completed isocrystal admitting an F^f-structure after finite extension k'/k. Construct the periodic filtered lift through 079–084 and then apply 075. The model and common period bound depend on the fixed rigid rank/determinant data.

items.name: Motivic realization after restriction to a curve
items.statement: Let C⊂X be a smooth complete-intersection curve of ample divisors, and spread it with the nice model. After shrinking and a finite residue-field extension, the F-overconvergent isocrystal restricted to C_s is, on a dense open C_s⁰, a subquotient of R^if_*O_(Y/Qp) for a projective family f:Y→C_s⁰. The family may depend on s. No motivicity theorem for all X is claimed.

items.name: Abe shtuka realization input
items.statement: For an irreducible finite-determinant F-isocrystal M on a finite-field curve, the external input realizes p₁^*M∨⊗p₂^*M in shtuka cohomology and passes via a proper generically finite smooth-scheme cover, inseparable base change and restriction to a curve slice to the family in 086. This is the crystalline-coefficient Abe theorem, not merely the ℓ-adic Lafforgue correspondence of GS.6.

items.name: Crystalline p-adic representation of a rigid connection
items.statement: Associate ρ_i,s:π₁(X_K)→GL_r(W(F_(p^f))) using the mixed periodic flow and its crystalline realization. Record the chosen finite constant extension, integral lattice and period; taking the geometric restriction and proving rigidity are subsequent operations.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Absolute irreducibility and projective rigidity
items.statement: A field-valued GL_r representation is absolutely irreducible when it remains irreducible over an algebraic closure; for PGL_r use absence of invariant proper projective linear subspaces. For a finitely generated abstract group, construct the finite-type PGL_r character moduli and call an isolated stable point rigid.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Continuous fixed-determinant deformation functor
items.statement: For an absolutely irreducible continuous Γ→GL_r(F), F a topological field, assign to a finite-dimensional local F-algebra A continuous lifts with the prescribed residual isomorphism class, modulo the specified conjugacy relation, AND keep the determinant fixed for this paper's rigidity claims. Artinian corepresentability is the rigidity condition. The explicit missing determinant clause in Definition 5.2 is E4.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Integral residual rigidity convention
items.statement: For a local field F with integers O_F, the paper calls an O_F-representation rigid and absolutely irreducible when its reduction over the residue field has both properties. This convention is stronger than simply saying the generic-fibre representation is rigid; preserve the distinction when reading Theorem 5.4.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: GL rigidity versus projective rigidity
items.statement: For a finitely generated abstract Γ and irreducible characteristic-zero representation over algebraically closed K, fixed-determinant GL rigidity is equivalent to PGL rigidity. Scalar character twists account for one direction; the reverse requires lifting the µ_r obstruction over the chosen henselian/formal deformation ring. Unrestricted GL rigidity would make rank one a counterexample.

items.name: Profinite completion and finite-coefficient rigidity
items.statement: For ρ:π₁^top(X)→GL_r(F_q) absolutely irreducible with fixed determinant, the associated continuous representation of the profinite completion is rigid iff its fixed-determinant Betti moduli point is isolated. Prove the bijection on finite Artin-coefficient representations and identify the formal completion. State the PGL counterpart separately as the same proof with projective conjugacy.

items.name: Projective arithmetic descent of a rigid representation
items.statement: For a rigid absolutely irreducible projective representation of π₁^top(X) defined over the localized number-field lattice in §5, after a finite Galois extension of the arithmetic model's function field its prime-to-M profinite realization extends to π₁(X_L). Construct the Galois stabilizer and extension data; invariance of a conjugacy class alone is not an arbitrary GL lifting theorem.

items.name: Faltings small p-adic Simpson correspondence
items.statement: For K a p-adic local field with valuation ring V and X a proper V-scheme with the toroidal hypotheses of [Fa2], construct the equivalence between small Higgs bundles and small generalized geometric representations, retaining the chosen lift and coefficient-completion conventions. The Qp-theory's nilpotent Higgs fields are small; deformations stay in the comparison range used to test rigidity.

items.name: Comparison of LSZ and Faltings realizations
items.statement: For a rigid periodic Higgs object, the geometric generic-fibre representation from LSZ corresponds under Faltings to a Frobenius shift σ^m of the original Higgs bundle. Prove this via the direct sum of all f shifts (period one), Faltings's crystalline example and identification of simple summands. Do not assert the shift m is zero or canonical.

items.name: Geometric absolute irreducibility of the realization
items.statement: For the ρ_i,s constructed from the nice model, restriction to π₁(X_Kbar) is absolutely irreducible in the source's coefficient convention, by matching a stable Higgs summand under the p-adic Simpson equivalence. Verify separately the residual convention of Definition 5.3 if that stronger assertion is exported.

items.name: Geometric rigidity of the realization
items.statement: The same geometric representation is rigid with its determinant fixed, via deformation-compatible Faltings comparison and rigidity of the shifted Higgs bundle. Generic-fibre rigidity alone does not prove rigidity of the residual representation; the interface between Definition 5.3 and the proof is an explicit completion gate.

items.name: Good primes: coefficient fields split
items.statement: For the finite collection of rigid rank-r representations, infinitely many primes p satisfy the coefficient-field embedding/splitting requirements, so the rigid W(F_q)-representations and their projectivizations in the stated family descend to Z_p. Apply Cassels to a finite-type subring of C containing all coefficients and relevant normalizations; using a normal closure makes complete splitting explicit. State the strengthened form needed by Theorem 6.1: the subring may also be enlarged by the inverse of any prescribed non-zero element of it, so that the resulting good closed point avoids that element's vanishing locus. Infinitude of residue characteristics alone does not make the good points meet every non-empty open of S; see E6.

items.name: Good primes: residual rigid points lift
items.statement: After excluding finitely many primes, every rigid absolutely irreducible residual representation in the fixed moduli problem is reduction of one of the chosen number-field models, and likewise projectively. Spread the finite isolated locus and exclude new vertical isolated components rather than asserting all representations lift.

items.name: Good primes: Witt points and arithmetic projective descent
items.statement: The Cassels embeddings can supply closed s with k(s)=F_p and a compatible model-function-field embedding into Q_p; for these s the projective rigid representations extend from geometric π₁ to π₁(X_Qp). Keep the chosen normalized arithmetic extension in the coefficient ring and invert ord(L).

items.name: Projective period one at good points
items.statement: At every good s, σ(V,θ) and (V,θ) are isomorphic as PGL_r-Higgs bundles. This is projective period one only; it does not identify the original GL_r objects without a scalar-line twist.

items.name: Zero Kodaira–Spencer field means unitary monodromy
items.statement: For a polarizable complex variation of Hodge structure underlying an irreducible flat connection on smooth projective complex X, the associated graded Higgs field is zero iff its monodromy is unitary. State the polarization/complex-VHS convention rather than assuming an integral structure.

items.name: Vanishing p-curvature implies unitarity for rigid connections
items.statement: In C, if a spread model has zero p-curvature at all closed points, the complex monodromy is unitary. At good primes, projective period one makes gr∇ scalar, and nilpotency over the reduced fibre makes that scalar zero. Deduce generic vanishing by constructing good points in every relevant nonempty open (E6), not merely counting infinitely many residue characteristics.

items.name: Integral versus strongly integral monodromy
items.statement: Integral means conjugate to a representation over the algebraic integers O_Qbar; strongly integral means a Z-lattice of the same representation is preserved. These are different predicates. Finite generation lets an integral representation be defined over O_L for one number field but does not make its single complex embedding discrete.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Strong integrality plus unitarity gives finite image
items.statement: A subgroup of GL_n(Z) contained, after conjugation, in a compact unitary group is finite, since it is discrete and bounded. This argument does not apply to one complex embedding of GL_n(O_L) when [L:Q]>1.

items.name: Integral unitary representation of infinite image
items.statement: Choose an algebraic unit α of modulus one that is not a root of unity (for example a unit-circle conjugate of a Salem number). On a genus≥1 surface send one standard generator to α and all others to 1. This gives an integral unitary rank-one representation of infinite image. Require α⁻¹ integral as well to land in GL₁(O_Qbar); this example is not a finite-determinant rigid connection.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Companion relation with coefficient isomorphism
items.statement: Over finite-field Y, for coefficient isomorphism τ between Qpbar and Qℓbar, or between two algebraically closed coefficient fields of the same type, define companionship by τ(det(1−tFrob_y|E_y))=det(1−tFrob_y|V_y) at every closed y. Fix the paper's crystalline absolute versus ℓ-adic geometric Frobenius translation and normalized iterated structure; do not require τ to be continuous.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: p-to-ell companions and Chebotarev uniqueness
items.statement: For smooth finite-field Y and irreducible finite-determinant overconvergent F-isocrystal E, the [AE] existence theorem supplies an irreducible ℓ-adic companion for ℓ≠p. Chebotarev on both sides gives uniqueness up to isomorphism and injectivity on isomorphism classes; verify the exact semisimple/geometric hypotheses and rank-one determinant-order compatibility.

items.name: Trace-free cohomology comparison on a lift
items.statement: For the proper smooth lift and the crystal coming from (E,∇), rational crystalline H¹ of End⁰ agrees with de Rham H¹ of the lifted connection, compatibly with the selected field embeddings and base changes. This is the coefficient comparison supplied by CR.2, not merely the pointwise Witt-vector isocrystal structure.

items.name: Finite cohomologically rigid comparison sets
items.statement: Fix r,d with p∤d and a constant extension ktilde(s) supporting the Frobenius constructions. Define S(r,d) from irreducible cohomologically rigid complex connections of determinant order d; S(s,p,r,d) from their constructed geometric isocrystals with Frobenius; and S(s,ℓ,r,d) from the matching irreducible lisse objects with H¹(End⁰)=0. Fix whether isomorphisms forget arithmetic Frobenius twists, and choose finite-order determinant normalizations before counting (G6).

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Companions remain geometrically irreducible
items.statement: For the companion V of a rigid isocrystal in S(s,p,r,d), V is geometrically irreducible, hence its pullback to the geometric characteristic-zero fibre is irreducible. Use finite-constant-extension compatibility, geometric irreducibility of the original object and surjectivity of specialization.

items.name: Companions preserve trace-free H1 vanishing
items.statement: For those companions, equality of local factors gives equality of L-functions for End⁰. Purity of weight zero and proper smooth cohomological weights isolate the weight-one eigenvalues, so crystalline and ℓ-adic H¹ dimensions agree. Proper smooth specialization identifies this with H¹ on the geometric generic fibre; the resulting group vanishes.

items.name: Companions preserve geometric determinant order
items.statement: In the normalized comparison family the determinant has geometric order exactly d and is unchanged by the permitted constant extensions. The rank-one companion construction and surjective geometric specialization preserve that exact order. An arbitrary arithmetic finite-order twist can lose order after constant extension, so the geometric convention must be enforced.

items.name: Betti realization bounds the companion count
items.statement: Pull back V along π₁^top(X)→π₁^ét(X), descend its finitely many matrix coefficients to a finite-type subring and embed into C. Analytic/étale and coefficient base-change comparisons give a cohomologically rigid fixed-determinant Betti point. Prove that this bounds the number of the geometric companion classes by #S(r,d).

items.name: Bijection from complex rigid objects to isocrystals
items.statement: With the precise comparison sets and normalization in 111, the construction of Theorem 1.6 is a bijection S(r,d)→S(s,p,r,d). Injectivity and finite counts must be established; no claim of a canonical Frobenius structure independent of choices is implicit.

items.name: Complete p-to-ell and ell-to-p correspondence in the rigid class
items.statement: For τ:Qpbar≃Qℓbar, companionship gives a bijection S(s,p,r,d)→S(s,ℓ,r,d); its inverse provides the τ⁻¹ crystalline companions in this class. This theorem concerns the cohomologically rigid family, not arbitrary lisse sheaves in higher dimension.

items.name: p-to-p companions permute the rigid set
items.statement: For σ:Qpbar≃Qpbar, choose τ,τ' with σ=(τ')⁻¹∘τ and compose the two established p-to-ℓ bijections to obtain σ-companions and a permutation of S(s,p,r,d). Prove independence from the intermediate ℓ/choices using local-polynomial uniqueness.

items.name: Cohomologically rigid SL3 is motivic
items.statement: For smooth projective complex X, a cohomologically rigid rank-three connection with trivial determinant is integral by [EG] and is of geometric origin by [LS]; the latter source realizes it through abelian families in the scope used here. Import the complex integrality interface from the pending HodgeStructuresPartII proposal rather than duplicating it.

items.name: Rank-three cohomologically rigid p-curvature conjecture
items.statement: For a cohomologically rigid rank-three connection of trivial determinant on smooth projective complex X, zero p-curvature on a suitable arithmetic model implies finite monodromy. Use the abelian-family motivicity result, connected motivic Galois group input and André's theorem with their exact hypotheses.

items.name: No symmetric differentials implies finite monodromy
items.statement: For smooth projective complex X with H⁰(X,Sym^iΩ¹)=0 for every i>0, all integrable connections have finite monodromy and are rigid in their fixed-data moduli problem, as supplied by [BKT] Theorem 0.1. The article cites this theorem; it does not prove it by the characteristic-p method.

items.name: Uniform zero-curvature premise for every rigid object
items.statement: Assume every cohomologically rigid connection on the fixed X admits an arithmetic model with zero p-curvature at all closed points. Then every such connection has finite monodromy: all conjugate coefficient embeddings remain cohomologically rigid and unitary, and restriction of scalars of an O_L-lattice is strongly integral. The universal premise over conjugate connections is essential; zero p-curvature of just one object is not substituted.

items.name: Infinitesimal conic scaling of a spectral support
items.statement: For V⊂T*Z' and n≥1, put V_n=V×Spec k[t]/(t−1)^n, with scaling map m induced by t on cotangent vectors and retraction r to V. On Hitchin coefficients the corresponding μ action is a_i↦t^i a_i, not uniform weight one on all coefficients.
items.locator: Appendix A, (A.1),(A.2), Remark A.1 pp.153–154; p.155

uses.where: Appendix A, (A.1),(A.2), Remark A.1 pp.153–154; p.155

items.name: Brauer class of the differential-operator algebra
items.statement: Construct the étale connecting map from the closed-one-form/Cartier exact sequence that sends the tautological form θ to [𝒟]. Prove naturality, additivity and the relative-base variant. Geometric Brauer classes, unlike field Brauer groups, require the sheaf/étale comparison and splitting torsors.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Infinitesimal scaling preserves the Brauer class
items.statement: For smooth projective W₂-liftable Z/k and a spectral support Z'_a of an integrable connection, the source asserts [m*𝒟]=[r*𝒟] on (Z'_a)_p. Retain this as a source theorem target with gate E5: the printed support argument confuses the parameter thickening with the cotangent zero-section and must be replaced by a valid relative Cartier/Brauer calculation.

items.name: Refined Morita equivalence under infinitesimal scaling
items.statement: With a chosen W₂-lift, refine 125 to an equivalence between the module categories of m*𝒟 and r*𝒟 on the thickened spectral support, using the compatible additive equivalence for D_(θ₁+θ₂) and D_θ₁⊗D_θ₂ from [BB]. Check its restriction at t=1 and coherence; equality of Brauer classes alone is not a canonical equivalence.

items.name: Deforming a connection along its scaled Hitchin invariant
items.statement: Under 125 and the corrected family BNR interface, construct an integrable connection on Z×Spec k[t]/(t−1)^p with invariant μ(a,t) restricting to the initial connection at t=1. Transport its module via the Morita equivalence, retaining local freeness and the normalized rank-r invariant.

items.name: Alternative large-prime nilpotency proof
items.statement: For a spread rigid complex connection with bounded local deformation length, the nonzero scaled Hitchin invariant produces infinitesimal deformations whose order grows with p; for large p this contradicts rigidity. This Appendix-A route avoids classical Simpson in the nilpotency proof but is gated by 125–127, not a verified independent workaround for E2/E3.

items.name: PD multiplicative scaling action
items.statement: From a W₂-lift construct the action of the PD hull of the identity in G_m on the connection category, as the de Rham counterpart to scaling Higgs fields. Specify its PD-base, functorial action and compatibility with finite infinitesimal truncations before using the remark as an input.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Small-prime nilpotency under cohomological rigidity
items.statement: For perfect k of characteristic p>2 and smooth projective W₂(k)-liftable Z, a stable cohomologically rigid flat connection has nilpotent p-curvature, as asserted by Corollary A.7. The proof must verify the fixed-determinant tangent convention, the action when p divides a Hitchin weight/rank, and Appendix-A gates; do not add a large-p assumption silently or claim its proof audited here.

items.name: Absolute Fontaine–Laffaille input
items.statement: Use the existing planned integral filtered Frobenius-module category over an absolutely unramified coefficient base and its Galois functor, with unrestricted torsion full faithfulness only in the normalized [0,p−2] range. Relative objects on Z_W, additional connection data and the flow comparison remain 073–074.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Overconvergent geometric coefficients
items.statement: Use the frame/descent definition of overconvergent F-isocrystals, including the rational coefficient convention, restriction to convergent objects and proper-case comparison. Neither ordinary p-adic completion nor a semilinear vector space by itself proves overconvergence.

uses.how: Used in the constructions and proof interfaces recorded in this item and its dependency consumers.

items.name: Proper smooth p-adic weight input
items.statement: For the overconvergent F-isocrystals in the paper's finite-field proper smooth setting, use the rigid trace formula and purity of H^i for weight-zero coefficients, with dual and Tate-twist conventions fixed. These isolate cohomological degrees in the alternating L-function expression.

items.name: Formal moduli completion interface
items.statement: For a constructed stable moduli point, identify its deformation functor with the formal completion of the moduli space, taking account of stabilizers, framing and determinant. Use algebraization only with its hypotheses; the article's application to rigid continuous representations consumes this generic interface.

items.name: Integrality of cohomologically rigid connections
items.statement: An irreducible cohomologically rigid complex local system with finite determinant on smooth projective X has integral monodromy: after conjugation its finitely generated image is defined over O_L for some number field L. This is the separate EG18 theorem cited in §8, with its nonproper quasi-unipotent extension outside the present specialization. Do not replace integrality by strong Z-integrality.

items.name: Geometric origin of a flat connection
items.statement: For the convention of Conjecture 1.3, geometric origin means that on a dense open U⊂X the connection is a subquotient of a Gauss–Manin connection R^if_*(O_Y,d) from a smooth projective family f:Y→U. Specify the comparison and chosen coefficient category. The definition does not assert existence of such a family for every rigid object.

uses.how: Distinguishes proved curve motivicity from the proposed higher-dimensional statement.
